description: Autoresearch Page — A dev-only dashboard for launching and analyzing parallel workflow architecture comparison runs with statistical A/B testing. Users select a workflow and a variation type (Architecture: Traditional vs Agentic Verification vs Multi-Agent Pipeline; Same: 3 identical runs for repeatability), then observe each entry's live status as workflows execute in isolated worktrees. When all entries complete, a structured metric comparison (success, iterations, duration_ms) and an AI-generated prose report identify the winning architecture with a confidence score. Comparison runs are stored in the comparison_runs PostgreSQL table and served via runner HTTP endpoints POST /comparison/start, GET /comparison/:id, GET /comparisons and Tauri commands under the qontinui_comparison plugin. This page surfaces the research infrastructure underlying architecture selection decisions.

groups.name: Page Structure & Layout
groups.description: The Autoresearch page is a dev-only tab rendered in the main content area. It displays a header with the page title and a launch button, a list of existing comparison runs, and a detail panel for the selected run.

assertions.description: A heading with text 'Autoresearch' or 'Architecture Research' is present at the top of the page
A button labeled 'New Comparison', 'Run Comparison', or 'Compare Architectures' (or with textContent containing 'Compare') is present and enabled on the page
When no comparison runs have been created, the page displays an empty state message explaining that no comparisons exist and prompting the user to start one by clicking the new comparison button
assertions.precondition: No comparison runs exist in the database

assertions.description: The page layout follows the standard runner dev-tab pattern: a compact header row with title and action buttons, a scrollable list of comparison runs on the left (or full-width), and a detail panel on the right (or below) when a run is selected. The page fills the full height of its container with overflow-auto.

groups.name: Workflow Selection
groups.description: Before starting a comparison, the user must select which unified workflow to run. The backend validates that the workflow exists in PostgreSQL via GET /unified-workflows/:id before accepting a POST /comparison/start request. The Tauri command start_comparison (plugin: qontinui_comparison) performs the same lookup before inserting the comparison_runs row.

assertions.description: A workflow selector (dropdown, combobox, search field, or list) is present in the launch form. It should show the user's available unified workflows by name. The selected workflow's ID is sent as workflow_id in the POST /comparison/start request body.

If the workflow is deleted after selection but before submission, the POST /comparison/start returns HTTP 404 with body {error: 'Workflow not found: <id>'}. The UI should display an inline error message such as 'Workflow not found' and not leave the user in a broken state.
assertions.precondition: A workflow that no longer exists is selected

assertions.description: The workflow list in the selector should be fetched from GET /unified-workflows or equivalent and show workflow names rather than raw IDs. After selecting a workflow, its ID (not name) is used as workflow_id in the comparison start request.

groups.name: Comparison Launch Form
groups.description: The launch form or dialog allows the user to configure a new comparison run: select a workflow, choose a variation type (architecture or same), and optionally toggle worktree isolation. Submitting posts to POST /comparison/start via the runner HTTP API or via the Tauri qontinui_comparison.start_comparison command.

assertions.description: The launch form includes a way to select the variation type. At minimum: 'Architecture' (compares Traditional vs Agentic Verification vs Multi-Agent Pipeline) and 'Same' (3 identical runs for repeatability). The selected variation type determines the entries created by the backend.

A checkbox or toggle labeled 'Worktree isolation' or 'Use worktree' is present in the launch form. When enabled, each comparison entry runs in its own git worktree (use_worktree=true in each entry's overrides). For architecture comparisons this defaults to enabled per the backend default_true() in StartComparisonRequest.

Clicking the launch/run button submits POST /comparison/start with {workflow_id, variation_type, use_worktree}. The backend responds with {data: {comparison_id: 'cmp-<uuid>', entries_count: 3}}. The UI should immediately show the new comparison in the list with status 'running' and entries in 'pending' state, then poll for updates. Alternatively the Tauri command qontinui_comparison.start_comparison returns the comparison_id string.
assertions.precondition: A workflow is selected and a variation type is chosen

assertions.description: When the 'Architecture' variation type is selected, the backend creates exactly 3 entries: label='Traditional' (overrides: {workflow_architecture: 'traditional', use_worktree: true}), label='Agentic Verification' (overrides: {workflow_architecture: 'agentic_verification', use_worktree: true}), and label='Multi-Agent Pipeline' (overrides: {workflow_architecture: 'multi_agent_pipeline', use_worktree: true}). The launched comparison should display all three entry labels.
assertions.precondition: Architecture variation type was selected and comparison was launched

assertions.description: When the 'Same' variation type is selected, the backend creates exactly 3 entries: label='Run 1', label='Run 2', label='Run 3'. All three use identical config overrides ({use_worktree: <user_choice>}). This tests workflow repeatability and non-determinism.
assertions.precondition: Same variation type was selected and comparison was launched

groups.name: Comparison Run List
groups.description: The page lists recent comparison runs fetched from GET /comparisons (up to 50 most recent, returned as an array of ComparisonRunView). Each run shows its ID (or short ID), workflow ID, variation type, status, and creation date. The list is the primary navigation surface for entering a run's detail view.

assertions.description: When comparison runs exist, the list renders one item per comparison run. Each item is clickable or selectable to open the detail view for that run.
assertions.precondition: At least one comparison run exists

assertions.description: Each comparison run item displays a status badge: 'running' (green or blue with animation), 'comparing' (yellow — AI analysis in progress), 'completed' (blue or green checkmark), or 'failed' (red). The badge reflects the current value of the status field in ComparisonRunView.
assertions.precondition: At least one comparison run exists

assertions.description: Each comparison run item shows its variation type ('architecture', 'same', or 'custom'), allowing users to distinguish architecture comparison runs from repeatability tests.
assertions.precondition: At least one comparison run exists

assertions.description: A 'Refresh' button or icon button is present near the list. Clicking it re-fetches comparison runs from GET /comparisons and updates statuses. Running comparisons should also be auto-polled periodically (every 5–15 seconds) to show live progress without requiring manual refresh.

groups.name: Running Comparison Detail View
groups.description: When a comparison run with status 'running' is selected, the detail view shows all entries and their individual live statuses. Entry statuses are fetched from GET /comparison/:id which enriches the stored entries with live task_run statuses from PostgreSQL. Entries transition from 'pending' → 'running' → 'completed'/'failed' as workflow runs progress.

assertions.description: The detail panel for a running comparison shows a list of all entries (e.g., Traditional, Agentic Verification, Multi-Agent Pipeline for architecture variation) each with their current status badge: 'pending' (not yet launched), 'running' (workflow executing), 'completed' (workflow done successfully), or 'failed' (workflow failed or stopped).
assertions.precondition: A running comparison run is selected

assertions.description: Each entry that has been launched (status 'running' or 'completed') should show its task_run_id and ideally a clickable link to navigate to the corresponding task run in the Active or History tab. The task_run_id is populated after the background task calls POST /unified-workflows/:id/run for each entry.

target.label: Entry list with task run IDs

assertions.precondition: A running comparison is selected and at least one entry has been launched

assertions.description: While a comparison run is selected and its status is 'running', the detail view automatically polls GET /comparison/:id every 5–15 seconds to update entry statuses without requiring a manual refresh. The GET handler enriches entries with live task_run statuses and auto-transitions to 'completed' when all_done=true.
assertions.precondition: A running comparison is selected in the detail view

groups.name: Completed Comparison Detail — Results Overview
groups.description: When a comparison run completes (status='completed'), the detail view shows the full result breakdown: per-entry results (success/fail, iteration count, duration_ms), the AI comparison report, and the AI recommendation with confidence score. The completed_at timestamp is shown. Status auto-transitions to 'completed' when the GET /comparison/:id handler detects all_done=true.

assertions.description: Each completed comparison entry shows its three result metrics from ComparisonEntryResultJson: success (pass/fail indicator), iterations (number of workflow sessions — from task_run.sessions_count), and duration_ms (computed from created_at and completed_at of the task_run). Failed entries show success=false with iterations and duration still populated if available.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run is selected

assertions.description: The detail view shows an 'AI Report' or 'Comparison Report' section containing a prose AI-generated analysis of the results. This is the report field (TEXT) from the comparison_runs table, populated by AI comparison analysis after all entries complete. The section should be visually distinct from the metric table.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with a non-null report is selected

assertions.description: The detail view shows a 'Recommendation' section displaying the ComparisonRecommendation: branch_name (the winning variant label), confidence as a percentage (0–100%, derived from the confidence f64 field which is 0.0–1.0), and the reasoning prose text.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with a non-null recommendation is selected

assertions.description: The AI comparison report should contain the names of the compared architectures ('Traditional', 'Agentic Verification', 'Multi-Agent Pipeline' for architecture variation) and evaluate them on success, speed (iterations + duration), and overall effectiveness. For variation_type='same', the report instead analyzes run-to-run variance and repeatability — whether the three runs produced consistent results.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with a report is selected

groups.name: Structured Metric Analysis
groups.description: The page displays machine-readable metric comparisons across variants from StructuredComparisonReport (built by build_structured_report in comparison.rs). The HTTP API surfaces three metrics per completed entry from ComparisonEntryResultJson: success (bool → 1.0/0.0, higher=better), iterations (u32, lower=better), and duration_ms (u64, lower=better). A winner is identified by which variant wins the most metrics, with a confidence score expressed as winner_wins / total_metrics (0.0–1.0).

assertions.description: A metrics comparison table or cards section shows the three tracked metrics for each variant side-by-side: success (1=passed/0=failed, higher=better), iterations (lower=better), and duration_ms (lower=better). For each metric, the best-performing variant is visually highlighted (e.g., bold, green, or a 'best' indicator).
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with at least 2 completed entries is selected

assertions.description: The page prominently displays the winning variant (the one with the most 'best' metric wins out of the 3 tracked metrics) with a confidence score as a percentage. The winner is the StructuredComparisonReport.winner field; confidence is StructuredComparisonReport.confidence × 100.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with at least 2 completed entries is selected

assertions.description: Each metric row in the comparison table shows the delta_pct between best and worst variants, computed by build_metric_delta: ((max - min) / |min|) × 100, or 100 if min=0 and max>0, or 0 if both are 0. For example: Traditional=5 iterations, Agentic=3 → delta_pct = ((5-3)/3)×100 = 66.7%. A high delta_pct indicates a strong performance differentiator between the variants.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison with 2+ completed entries is selected

assertions.description: A p-value or 'Statistical significance' indicator may be shown. The StructuredComparisonReport.p_value is always None in the current build_structured_report (comment: 'Requires multiple trials per variant'). When p_value is null or absent, the page should display 'N/A' or omit the field entirely, optionally with a tooltip 'Requires multiple trials per variant'.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run is selected

assertions.description: The StructuredComparisonReport includes a cost_breakdown field: a list of (label, cost_proxy) pairs where cost_proxy = duration_ms / 1000.0 (duration in seconds used as a cost proxy). If displayed, the page should label this clearly as an estimate or proxy, not a real dollar cost.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with at least 2 entries is selected

groups.name: Comparison Algorithm Correctness
groups.description: The winner and confidence in StructuredComparisonReport are derived by a specific algorithm in build_structured_report (comparison.rs): winner = variant with the most metric wins (tie-broken by highest success_rate); confidence = winner_metric_wins / total_metrics_count (0.0–1.0). With 3 metrics, valid confidence values are 0.33, 0.67, or 1.0. An AI verification workflow can check that displayed winner and confidence match these formulas applied to the visible metric values.

assertions.description: The displayed winner should be verifiable from the metric table: count how many of the 3 metrics each variant wins (success: higher=better; iterations, duration_ms: lower=better). The variant winning the most is the winner. Tie-break: higher success_rate wins. If the displayed winner does not match this count, build_structured_report has a bug.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with at least 2 completed entries is displayed

assertions.description: The displayed confidence percentage should equal (winner_metric_wins / 3) × 100. With 3 metrics: 33% = wins 1/3, 67% = wins 2/3, 100% = wins 3/3. A confidence value that is not one of these three discrete values (for 3-metric comparisons) indicates a calculation bug in build_structured_report.
assertions.precondition: A completed comparison run with at least 2 completed entries is displayed

assertions.description: For variation_type='architecture': exactly 3 entries labeled 'Traditional', 'Agentic Verification', and 'Multi-Agent Pipeline'. For variation_type='same': exactly 3 entries labeled 'Run 1', 'Run 2', 'Run 3'. For variation_type='custom': entry count equals the number of elements in the custom_overrides array sent at launch. A mismatch in count or labels is a backend entry-creation bug.
assertions.precondition: A comparison run is selected

assertions.description: For a 'same' variation comparison (3 identical runs: Run 1, Run 2, Run 3), the metric analysis reveals non-determinism. If success, iterations, or duration_ms vary significantly between runs, the workflow has reliability issues. The page should indicate that the goal is repeatability — ideally all three entries show identical success and similar iteration counts and durations. A high delta_pct on a 'same' comparison signals a non-determinism problem.
assertions.precondition: A completed 'same' variation comparison run is selected

groups.name: Comparison Status Lifecycle
groups.description: The page correctly reflects the status progression for comparison runs: running (entries launching and executing) → completed (all entries done, auto-transitioned by GET /comparison/:id when all_done=true). The 'comparing' status is a valid enum variant but requires a separate AI analysis pipeline to be set — the GET endpoint does not set it automatically. Failed state is shown when all entries fail on launch.

assertions.description: A comparison in 'running' state shows a progress indicator (spinner, animation, or 'Running' badge) and displays each entry's live status. The user can see which entries are 'pending' (not yet launched by the background task), 'running' (workflow executing), 'completed', or 'failed' in real time.
assertions.precondition: A 'running' comparison run is selected

assertions.description: A comparison in 'completed' state shows a 'Completed' badge, the created_at and completed_at timestamps (formatted as human-readable date/time), the metric analysis section, the AI report section (if report is not null), and the recommendation section (if recommendation is not null).
assertions.precondition: A 'completed' comparison run is selected

assertions.description: A comparison with status 'failed' shows a 'Failed' badge with red styling. A comparison is marked 'failed' by the background launch task when ALL entries fail immediately (all_failed=true in launch_comparison_entries). Individual entries that failed show their failure status. The user should see an indication of what went wrong if possible.
assertions.precondition: A 'failed' comparison run is selected

assertions.description: The comparison status lifecycle: (1) POST /comparison/start returns immediately with status='running', all entries status='pending'; (2) background task (launch_comparison_entries) calls POST /unified-workflows/:id/run for each entry, updating entries to status='running' with their task_run_ids; (3) as workflows complete, GET /comparison/:id enriches entry statuses from live task_run records; (4) when all entries are done (completed or failed), the GET handler auto-transitions comparison to 'completed' via pg.complete_comparison_run(). The page should reflect each of these transitions via polling.

groups.name: Research Configuration (Multi-Trial, Aspirational)
groups.description: Beyond single-shot comparisons, the ResearchConfig data structure in comparison.rs defines multi-trial experiment parameters: trials_per_experiment, search_dimensions (model, multi_agent_mode, max_iterations, context_tokens, workflow_architecture, custom), mutation_strategy (sequential/random_perturbation/ai_guided), and acceptance_criteria. If this advanced configuration UI is implemented, it should surface these fields. Currently the HTTP API only supports single-trial comparisons and p_value is always null.

assertions.description: If implemented, the page includes a section or panel for configuring multi-trial research experiments. At minimum: a 'trials_per_experiment' numeric input (number of runs per variant, default 1) and an acceptance_criteria section (primary metric selector with options: pass_rate, mean_iterations, mean_duration; significance_threshold numeric input). This section may be hidden behind an 'Advanced' disclosure.

If the research config panel is present, it should allow specifying search dimensions to vary across experiments: model (list of model IDs), multi_agent_mode (on/off), max_iterations (numeric range [min, max]), context_tokens (list of token limits), workflow_architecture (all 3 architectures), and custom (arbitrary JSON overrides per entry). At minimum 'workflow_architecture' and 'model' should be selectable.

The StructuredComparisonReport.p_value is always null in the current implementation (build_structured_report sets it to None). When multi-trial support is added: p_value should be computed for ≥2 trials per variant and displayed alongside the significance_threshold. For single-trial comparisons the page should show 'N/A — requires ≥2 trials per variant' rather than omitting the field entirely.

states.name: No Comparisons
states.description: No comparison runs have been created yet. The page shows an empty state message and the 'New Comparison' (or 'Compare') button.

transitions.name: Open launch form
transitions.description: Click the Compare / New Comparison button to open the launch form or panel

states.name: Comparison Run List
states.description: At least one comparison run exists. The page shows a scrollable list of runs, each with status badge, variation type, and creation metadata. A run can be selected to view its detail panel.

transitions.name: Select a comparison run
transitions.description: Click a comparison run item in the list to open its detail panel

transitions.name: Open launch form from list view
transitions.description: Click the Compare button to open the launch form while the list is visible

states.name: Launch Form Open
states.description: The launch form or dialog is open, allowing the user to select a workflow, choose a variation type, toggle worktree isolation, and submit to POST /comparison/start (or Tauri qontinui_comparison.start_comparison).

transitions.name: Cancel launch
transitions.description: Cancel the launch form without creating a comparison

transitions.name: Submit comparison run
transitions.description: Submit the form to POST /comparison/start. On success, the new comparison appears in the list and the detail view opens showing it in 'running' state with all entries 'pending'.

states.name: Comparison Detail View
states.description: A specific comparison run is selected. Its detail shows all entries with live statuses, and (if completed) the metric table, AI report, and recommendation.

transitions.name: Deselect comparison
transitions.description: Navigate back to the list view without a selected comparison (e.g., click a Back button or deselect the run in the list)
